title: Reduction of the specified integral exceptional counit
statement: Fix $D,C,E$, a smooth separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ of relative dimension $r$ between separated finite-type $D.k$-schemes, a normalized constructible exceptional coefficient system $S$ [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients], and its specified simultaneous purity family $A$ with target realization [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. For an integral finite-Tor input $K$, transport the actual exceptional counit by A.targetRealization and the actual left realization S.ring.left, obtaining $\epsilon_R:P_RG_RK\to K$. At each finite exponent $n+1$, its derived reduction is $Q_Y(\epsilon_R)=c_{G_RK}\,P_n(b_K)\,\epsilon_n$, in Lean composition order: first the canonical support comparison, then support of the canonical target reduction, then the specified finite exceptional counit [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Here $c$ is explicitly the reductionBridge, PurCompactSupport.comparison, finiteImageIso and inverse reductionBridge composite, and $b$ is purAdicTargetReduction [def-pur-adic-purity-objects]. This is an equality of actual morphisms for this normalized realization, not an assertion about arbitrary choices of adjoints.

proof.text:
use A.targetRealizationReductions to identify reduction of the inverse target
realization with the inverse of the prescribed exceptional mate. In the normalized
system S, the compact-support coefficient comparison and its exceptional mate satisfy
the counit equation. Map that equation through the full-category inclusions and
conjugate its scalar functors by their realization isomorphisms. Their naturality
cancels the intermediate realization maps. A.finiteRightNormalized identifies the
remaining finite exceptional realization with the ordinary etale adjoint, so its
counit is precisely smoothExceptionalCounit after the intrinsic equivalence.
The left realization S.ring.left gives the integral support term. On the finite
side, the same open and proper units identify it with finiteImageIso. Thus the
remaining composite is exactly c, followed by support of purAdicTargetReduction
and the finite exceptional counit. The finite-Tor hypothesis supplies boundedness
below, including the zero object and the empty scheme, so the totalized zero branch
of smoothExceptionalCounit is never used on a nonzero unbounded input.
